label: Whatever is desirable in a respect is PERFECT_1 in that respect
paraphrase: Backward half of 'each thing is desirable insofar as it is perfect', analyst weak version: for every bearer x and perfection p, if x is desirable in p then x is perfect in p (PERFECT_1). In ST I q.5 a.1 co. this half rests on the reading of secundum quod as a biconditional, not on the stated reason.

connection_plan.missing_bridge: The q.5 argument a5a50fe3 needs the biconditional (comparison conjunct 6). An independent argument for this backward half, for example from the object of appetite in ST I q.80 a.1, would together with the forward half give the premise; none is built.
connection_plan.blocker: The experience-machine verdict does not discriminate this half (controls rows 4 and 5), and no other argument for it is recorded.
